newsitem.title: USA: Utah lets Conoco drill for oil in monument area.
newsitem.headline: Utah lets Conoco drill for oil in monument area.

text.p: The state of Utah approved a permit for DuPont Co unit Conoco to drill for oil on a state lease in the Grand Staircase Escalante National Monument, a Conoco spokesman said Thursday.
The company does not know yet when it will begin drilling on the controversial lease in the Reese Canyon area of the national monument created by President Bill Clinton last year.
"First we have a lot of planning to complete, and we do not have a date to begin drilling," said spokesman John Bennitt in the company's Denver office.
Conoco estimates that the area could hold more than a hundred million barrels of oil reserves.
Local green groups have been trying stop the company from drilling on state and federal leases which it has held in the area for almost 10 years and were set to expire this year.
Conoco had been considering exploring for oil there for two years before Clinton set the land aside. When he named the monument he said valid existing leases would be honored.
"We are very pleased that the state of Utah in issuing the permit recognized the validity of our lease," Bennitt said.
"We are going to be very careful about working in this area because of its obvious sensitivity," he said.
The company has an application pending with the U.S. Bureau of Land Management to drill on a federal lease in the area.
When the company applied last month to drill on the federal lease, Conoco officials said they had made the request to test how the government would respond.

The company had sought to suspend the lease so it would not lose it at the end of 10 years, but the Bureau of Land Management said Conoco would have to file an application before the agency would consider suspending the lease.
